answers.value: Scope = the candidate capability/epic under discovery; assess feasibility across the affected systems (Guidewire policy/claims/billing, integration layer, data platform) named in the epic's architecture context in Jira.
Discovery/elaboration phase for the epic, completed before the epic enters a sprint (typically 1-2 sprints ahead).

Feasibility record captures: affected systems/CMDB CIs, integration points, estimated complexity (T-shirt or story-point range), key technical risks, and required non-functional constraints; no field left as TBD before ARB review.
Every dependency/system named in the feasibility note reconciles to a CMDB CI or a documented external service; count of named systems = count of linked CIs.
Feasibility findings recorded as an ADR + spike report attached to the epic in Jira, versioned with author and date; retained for the life of the initiative.
Open technical risks logged as Jira risk items with owner and mitigation; any 'not feasible as scoped' finding routes back to Product Owner for re-scoping via a documented decision.
Estimation/complexity methodology (reference-class story pointing + risk-adjusted T-shirt sizing) documented and approved by the Tech Lead; version noted on the feasibility record.
Sensitivity: if effort estimate varies >30% under best/worst-case assumptions, the epic is flagged high-uncertainty and requires a de-risking spike before commitment.
Materiality: initiatives estimated above 20 story points or touching >=2 core systems require formal ARB review before build.
All feasibility records produced this quarter for epics entering the backlog; sampled for completeness and dependency accuracy.
Pass = feasibility record complete (all mandatory sections), dependencies reconciled to CMDB, and ARB/Tech Lead sign-off present; fail = missing sections or unlinked dependencies.

Incomplete feasibility routes the epic back to discovery; proceeding to build without sign-off requires a 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with 10-business-day remediation SLA.
Acceptance = documented feasibility verdict (feasible / feasible-with-conditions / not-feasible), complexity range, risk list, and dependency map, reviewed by Tech Lead and (where material) ARB.
ADR + spike report stored in the epic's Jira/Confluence space; ARB decision recorded in the architecture governance register.

answers.value: Scope = SAST over all first-party source in the release repos and DAST over the deployed application in the staging environment; SCA over all third-party dependencies; population = every service/repo in the release train plus running endpoints exposed by the app.

All release repos (SAST/SCA) and all externally-reachable endpoints in staging (DAST); sampled with a known-vulnerable canary to confirm detection.

Acceptance = scans executed with current rulesets on the full scope, all critical/high triaged, and the security quality gate green (or all exceptions formally approved) before release.
Scan results and gate status attached to the PR checks and the release change ticket in the ITSM/security ticketing system; SARIF stored in the compliance evidence repository.

answers.value: Scope = unit tests for all new and changed code paths in the pull request; population = every changed public method and branch in the diff for the service/repo under change.
Authored with the code change; executed on every commit locally and on every pull request in CI; coverage gate evaluated per PR.
Each test has clear arrange/act/assert, meaningful name, and asserts behavior not implementation; no changed public method left untested; tests deterministic (no reliance on wall-clock/network).
Coverage reconciles: line coverage >=80% overall and >=90% on critical paths; coverage on changed lines >=80% (enforced by the PR coverage diff); test count increases with new public methods.
JUnit/coverage (Cobertura/LCOV) reports published as CI artifacts retained 90 days, tagged with commit SHA; coverage trend tracked in SonarQube by build.

Coverage below threshold fails the PR; a documented shortfall is allowed only via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day plan to raise coverage; flaky tests quarantined and fixed within 5 days.
All changed code paths in the PR diff; verified against a mutation-testing sample on critical modules to confirm assertion strength.
Pass = all unit tests green, line coverage >=80% (>=90% critical paths), changed-line coverage >=80%; fail = any red test or coverage below threshold on changed code.
Failing tests block merge; coverage shortfall blocks merge unless waived via 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager; flaky specs labeled 'flaky' with a 5-business-day fix SLA.
Acceptance = new/changed public methods covered, suite green, and coverage thresholds met on changed lines, verified by the CI coverage gate and PR review.
Coverage report + test results attached to the PR check and archived in the CI system; coverage badge/trend visible in SonarQube for the repo.

Materiality/tolerance = minimum 80% line coverage overall, 90% on critical paths, and >=80% on changed lines per PR; any drop below these tolerances fails the build and requires an approved 'SDLC-Exception' with a remediation plan.
